newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 28.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- New Aspiration Party leader Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has ruled out working with the Democrat party in a coalition government, saying he could no longer tolerate his arch-rival's criticism. The Democrats reportedly criticised the New Aspiration Party for creating national disunity by touting Chavalit as premier of the Northeast. (BANGKOK POST)

- Thailand today rolls out the red carpet for Britain's head of state Queen Elizabeth II who is the guest of their majesties the King and Queen. Queen Elizabeth and Prince Philip will be greeted by the Thai King and Queen on arrival. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- Police have set up special surveillance around two men arrested in Thailand in July in connection with a record heroin seizure in the United States following their efforts to bribe Thai authorities to escape extradition. Police say Li Yun-chung, or Phongsak Rojjanasakkul, and Cha Chung-chang, alias Praphan Thongchaisawang, offered up to 40 million baht in bribe to avoid extradition. (THE NATION)

- While fears are rising about mercury contamination in the Gulf of Thailand, another toxic heavy metal has been found in larger quantities in marine life and has caused some Thai fishery exports to be rejected by foreign countries. Fisheries Department researchers have revealed that the marine life in the Gulf is contaminated by cadmium, which is known to cause severe kidney damage to humans and is associated with other diseases such as weakening, anemia and heart disease. (THE NATION)

- The Finance Ministry will propose to the Cabinet tomorrow that provident funds form part of the requirements for registration of a company. Presently, the government can only require state enterprises to set up provident funds but there is not yet a law requiring private companies to establish them. (KRUNG THEP THURAKIJ)

- Petrochemical, education and health businesses will get the biggest share of the International Finance Corp's US$200 million investment in Thailand next year. The World Bank's private investment arm has already spent $500 million to take equity in Thai assets projected to grow in value by 20-40 percent next year. (BANGKOK POST)

- Thailand has urged members of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum to start cutting tariffs after 2000, but the reduction rate structure has not yet been specified. Thailand has broadly proposed tearing down its tariff barriers in two phrases, one between 1997 and 2000 and the second between 2001 and 2020. (THE NATION)
